The antennae snap erect on the same frame as the chest reaching full extension. Everything the world does arrives late: the rim's spring-back and the falling gold land after his stance is set, and the blossom keeps nodding and the branch keeps swinging on their own slower rhythms into the end of the shot. Wings fast and continuous throughout, including while he is buried.

widen off his body as he hauls up into the stance
shots.gagStaysVisible: his legs and both beating wings above the petal line, kicking
shots.gagContactAndWeight: His head and shoulders are wedged past the petal rim so the bloom takes his full weight and bows on its stem; each kick rocks the whole flower; his shoulders shove the rim wide as he hauls out and the rim springs back and dumps the flower's own loose gold onto his face and chest.
shots.gagPayoffShape: Two legs kicking above a flower rim — the impact told entirely by its residue — paid off by a caked bee erupting into a proud stance.
gagProhibitedStaging: never show the branch strike or the tumble — this shot begins after them

shots.purpose: Her eye-roll with the smile inside it — deliberately cut short, so the audience is denied the long hold the last one gave them and the energy has nowhere left to climb.
shots.audienceExperience: The child gets a flicker of the funny bee-look and it is snatched away. The parent sees the smile living inside the roll — she is enjoying him and will not be caught at it.
shots.openingImage: Level with Zenny in the flat, unmoving grammar, background soft green haze — the roll already in progress, her eyes travelling up and away from the direction he is in, the smile visible only at the corner of her mouth.
shots.principalPerformance: The roll is the smile's hiding place: eyes up and away, one corner lifting a fraction, then she puts it away and her attention returns to her sacks. Almost nothing moves except what she is thinking.
shots.cameraRelationship: Her frame stays flat and unmoved as before — the collision of grammars depends on her never breathing — but this time it is taken away from her early, at the moment the smile shows, so the picture leaves before the reaction has finished. What is alive inside the stillness is the roll travelling and the corner of the mouth losing the argument.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: For a fraction of a second she is caught enjoying him, and the shot is pulled before she can compose herself — the payoff the audience was trained to expect is withheld.
shots.closingImage: Zenny mid-roll, eyes up and off, one corner of her mouth lifted, her paws still resting on her full pollen sacks in the flat green haze — the picture leaving her before her face has settled.
shots.transitionReason: A cut to her buys altered power and is the shape the audience has been taught to expect; the point is that this one is cut short, and that only works as a separate, deliberately brief frame — folding her into his shot would forfeit both the expectation and the denial.
shots.cutPaceReason: The whole idea is one unbroken glimpse taken away too soon — any internal cut would give this frame more architecture than the beat is willing to grant it.
shots.physicalPerformance: Her paws keep their light hold on the full sacks, one thumb pressing and releasing the packed gold in a slow idle rhythm she never interrupts, while her eyes travel up and away from his direction in one continuous unhurried arc — the head following a degree or two behind them and no further. As the eyes reach the top of the arc one corner of her mouth lifts a fraction and her shoulders drop the smallest amount with the breath she lets out. She begins to draw the corner back down, and the picture is taken away from her before she gets there.
shots.animationTiming: One slow travelling arc, about a second and a half from start to top, with the head lagging a beat behind the eyes so the roll reads as thought rather than gesture. The mouth-corner lift is late and small, arriving only at the end of the arc, and it takes longer to appear than a smile would — it is leaking, not breaking. The thumb's idle press-and-release runs underneath the whole shot at its own unhurried pace and is still going when the cut takes her, mid-correction, a beat earlier than the audience expects.

shots.purpose: The point of view shears: the camera's attention reaches the darkening sky a half-beat before Fuzzby's hover goes crooked, so the audience's dread precedes his — the one place in the scene we know more than he does. Carries his annexing of the thunder.
shots.audienceExperience: The parent's stomach turns first, at a colour in the deep background behind the play. The child is still waiting for the next bonk and gets a crooked hover and a bee taking credit for thunder instead — funny, but the picture has gone cooler and slower and they feel it without a word being said.
shots.openingImage: Bee-height inside the flower corridor with Fuzzby small in the mid-ground still mid-dive, and the frame's attention already drifting up past him toward a canopy gap where the far background haze has gone grey-green — the play continuing beneath the part of the picture we are looking at.
shots.principalPerformance: The body betrays him before he decides anything: the hover tilts crooked, altitude sagging then over-correcting, and then he annexes the sound into the act — chest still half-pumped, because deflating would be admitting something, the line delivered as if he had cued the weather.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera anticipates for the first and only time in the scene: it goes to the weather ahead of both bees, then comes back down to Fuzzby late and finds his hover already crooked. The travel is slower and longer than anything before it — the thunder is lengthening the shots from the outside — and the cooling must live in the deep background behind the play, never in a fresh master; the treatment refuses a re-establishing wide here and so do I.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: The scene stops being about pollen. The sky darkens in the far background, his hover goes crooked on its own, and he converts the threat into material for the act without ever registering it as a threat.
shots.closingImage: Fuzzby hanging at a crooked tilt in thinning gold light, chest still half-pumped, caked face turned proudly out along the corridor, with the far background behind the canopy gap noticeably cooler and greyer than the leaves around him.
shots.transitionReason: Cutting away from her unfinished reaction into a frame that is already looking at the sky is what shears the point of view — continuing from her would keep us inside the comedy's rhythm at the exact moment the scene needs the audience to start looking past the play.
shots.cutPaceReason: The beat's tempo shape slows the scene from the outside, so the shot needs the drift up to the weather and the late return to his crooked hover to be two distinct movements of attention — two, and slow, not four; the thunder is lengthening shots, not chopping them.
shots.physicalPerformance: He is still working the dive when the rumble arrives, and his body takes it before his mind does: one whole side of his flight drops away so he hangs crooked, the altitude sagging low and then over-correcting too high in a single porpoise he never asked for, the caked face swinging as the tilt swings him. The correction does not fix him — he stays canted, hunting a level he cannot find with small quick wing adjustments. Then he takes ownership of it: the chest re-inflates to half its parade extension, the shoulders drag back, the head lifts and turns proudly out along the corridor, and he puts the line out as though the weather were a cue he had given — one antenna still riding the aftershock of the tilt while the other snaps up to match the claim. He never once looks at the sky.
shots.animationTiming: The slowest shot in the scene so far, and deliberately so. The drift up to the weather takes its own unhurried time before anything happens to him. The tilt arrives suddenly — a fast drop of one side — then everything after it decelerates: the sag is slow, the over-correction slower, and the canted hunting continues underneath the rest of the shot rather than resolving. The chest's re-inflation builds over about a second, and the line lands at the top of it, late, after the audience has already read the sky. The lagging antenna's aftershock settles last of all, a beat behind the claim. Wings fast and continuous throughout the tilt, the sag and the hold — the hover is crooked, never stalled.
internalCuts: drift the frame up past him to the canopy gap and hold on the grey-green far haze
come back down to find his hover already canted and hunting for a level

shots.purpose: Same stimulus, opposite grammar: her eyes reach the sky before her body moves and she names it flat and small — the warning underplayed so the thunder feels bigger.
shots.audienceExperience: The child hears the smallest, calmest sentence in the scene and it lands heavier than any crash. The parent watches her haze cool behind her while her own leaf stays warm, and knows nobody in this meadow is ready.
shots.openingImage: Level with Zenny in her flat unmoving grammar, her eyes already up at the sky while the rest of her has not moved at all — her leaf and her sacks still in warm gold, and the green haze behind her cooling and thickening toward grey.
shots.principalPerformance: Her eyes arrive at the sky before any part of her body follows, which is her whole grammar in one gesture; then the warning comes out flat and small, no enlargement, no volume, and she does not look toward him after saying it. She goes narrower rather than bigger under pressure.
shots.cameraRelationship: Still level with her and still refusing to move, because her frame is the only stillness the scene ever buys and this is the moment it is worth most. Stillness here is FOR the size of the thing she is naming: the smaller and flatter the frame, the bigger the sky. What lives inside it is the cooling of the haze behind her, the dust in the shaft going dull, and her eyes holding on something above the top of frame while her paws stay on her work.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: The weather is named for the first time, and the naming costs her nothing visible — which is what makes it land. Her warmth is going out of the background even as she stays warm in it.
shots.closingImage: Zenny level in the unmoved frame, eyes still up above the top of the picture, paws resting on her full sacks, her own leaf warm gold while the haze behind her has gone thick grey-green.
shots.transitionReason: The whole beat is one stimulus producing two opposite behaviours, and that comparison only exists across a cut — holding them in one travelling frame would blend the two grammars the treatment welds together and never blends.
shots.cutPaceReason: Her register is deadpan economy and the thunder has slowed the scene from outside; a cut inside this frame would add motion to the one shot whose entire value is that the picture has stopped while the sky gets bigger.
shots.physicalPerformance: Her eyes have already gone up above the top of frame and they stay working up there — tracking something crossing above her, one small re-aim as it moves, while every other part of her keeps doing what it was doing: her paws resting on the packed gold of her own sacks, her weight held forward on the leaf, her breathing gone shallower and slower than the shot before. The line comes out of a mouth that moves and a body that does not follow it, level and small, and her eyes never come down off the sky for it. Afterwards her forelegs draw a fraction closer to her body and the antennae angle back a degree — the whole response is a narrowing, and she never turns toward him. The leaf under her takes one small dip and recovers as her weight shifts.
shots.animationTiming: The stillest and longest-feeling shot in the scene, and every second of it has something small alive in it. The eyes are already up when the cut lands — no travel to watch, the movement has already happened, which is the economy. The single re-aim of the gaze comes early and is tiny. The line is delivered on one flat unhurried tempo with no accent anywhere in it, and a long beat sits after it before anything else happens. The narrowing — forelegs in, antennae back — takes place slowly across that beat, almost too slow to catch. The leaf's dip and recovery is the last motion in the shot, and behind her the haze thickens continuously from the first frame to the last, on a rate slower than any performance beat, so the world changes faster than she does.

shots.purpose: The boast IS the launch — and the flower has the last word, closing on him. The only impact with no ride before it, and the only one he cannot cover up, because the cover-up is stuck inside a bloom.
shots.audienceExperience: The child laughs hardest here: a bee gets eaten by a flower and his bottom is still wagging. The parent is looking past him at the wrong-coloured sky and the laugh has something cold underneath it — the two doors, in the same frame.
shots.openingImage: Bee-height in the corridor with Fuzzby driving forward into the shot from behind the lens, chest pumped on the boast, and dead ahead of him in the mid-ground an open flower waiting wide — cooling grey-green haze filling the corridor beyond it, gold light thinning across the petals.
shots.principalPerformance: He answers the warning with a boast and the boast has a throttle in it — the pumped chest drives him forward on a line he never levels, straight at the bloom, because for him a claim and a launch are the same movement. There is no anticipation of impact and no correction; he is the last to know, as always.
shots.cameraRelationship: The camera is his wingman one final time — towed forward on his drive, close and late, and it stays with the flower after he has gone into it rather than following him inside; the petals fold across the lens's view of him and the frame simply keeps watching the closed bloom. Then it lets the far background carry the cost: the cooled sky behind the canopy stays small and sharp in the depth of the same frame, never re-established, and her leaf is never revisited — she does not turn to look and the camera does not go to ask her.
shots.physicalOrEmotionalChange: One cause relayed: the boast drives him forward — his own speed carries him past the flower's centre — the impact folds the petals inward — and the fold clamps and holds, so only his rear half and two beating wings stay outside. Gold dust settles around him in cooling light and the petals do not open.
shots.closingImage: A single flower's petals closed tight around Fuzzby with only his rear half and two beating wings sticking out, gold dust settling around him in cooling grey-green light, the stem still swaying from the hit — and small and sharp in the far background behind the canopy, the sky already the wrong colour.
shots.transitionReason: Her flat warning has to be allowed to finish and land before his answer arrives, and the collision of the two grammars requires the boast to begin in his moving frame, not to grow out of her still one — cutting is what makes his answer read as an interruption of the weather rather than a reply to it.
shots.cutPaceReason: The tempo is slow-slow-snap-shut: one tightening reframe onto the bloom as the petals take him gives the snap its impact and then the picture has nowhere else to go, so anything more would chop a beat whose whole job is to stop the scene dead.
shots.physicalPerformance: The claim and the launch are one movement in him: the chest pumps forward on the answer and the pump itself is what drives him, so he is already travelling as the words go out, antennae proud-erect, hind legs trailing, the line rising and dipping under him without ever levelling. He does not slow, does not look down the line and does not brake — the head and chest drive past the bloom's centre and compress its inner petals, and his own speed rolls the outer petals inward over his shoulders until they fold shut behind him and grip at his waist. What is left outside keeps insisting: his rear half wags side to side against the closed petals as he shoves forward at something he cannot reach, and both wings beat fast and continuous outside the fold, working against a flower that has already won. The wagging gets smaller but does not stop, and the petals do not open.
shots.animationTiming: Slow, slow, snap, shut. The drive is the only fast thing left in the scene — no anticipation, full speed from the first frame, faster than the cooling world around it. The petal fold is heavy and quick, taking his speed out of him in a fraction of a second, and the clamp lands as a hard stop with nothing after it. Then the shot decelerates completely: the rear-half wag runs at a diminishing rhythm, the wings keep their fast continuous beat over the top of it, the stem's sway damps out slowly, and the loose gold takes the rest of the shot to settle. The last thing to change in the frame is nothing in the foreground at all — it is the far background haze continuing to cool while his bottom is still working.

hold on the closed flower as the stem's sway damps out and his rear half keeps wagging
shots.gagStaysVisible: his rear half and both fast-beating wings outside the petal line
shots.gagContactAndWeight: His head and chest drive past the bloom's centre and compress its inner petals; the compression rolls the outer petals inward over his shoulders; they fold tight behind him and hold, gripping at his waist; the stem takes the whole impact and sways, shaking loose gold down over his exposed rear half and the two wings still working outside.
shots.gagPayoffShape: A flower with a bee's back half sticking out of it, wings still going, in light that has gone the wrong colour.
gagProhibitedStaging: never let the petals close over him completely
never let the flower appear to attack — his own speed causes the fold
never cut away to her or to a wide re-establish for the weather
never let him wriggle free or comment from inside — the world gets the last word

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby
voicePerformances.dramaticIntention: Broadcast to Zenny down the corridor that a professional is on the job — he wants her to hear the work being done before she can see it done badly.

voicePerformances.relationshipTarget: Zenny, working out of sight down the flower corridor — he is singing AT her, not to himself.
voicePerformances.emotionalEntry: Already mid-throttle — the song is running before the shot is, self-appointed and on-parade.
voicePerformances.emotionalExit: The last syllable knocked sideways by the leaf, still trying to hold the tune while the world takes his exit line.
voicePerformances.pace: Fast, staccato, marching — each BIZZY clipped, faster than a bee needs to sing, chasing his own zig-zag.
voicePerformances.rhythm: Two identical triplets, but the second is a fraction faster and a fraction higher than the first — the climb is in the voice as well as the flight; the trailing ellipsis is the leaf taking him mid-phrase, not a fade-out.
voicePerformances.pauses: One breath-sized gap only, at the comma, taken on the dip toward the blossom — it is the loading action, the same beat his body uses to aim.
voicePerformances.breaths: A big showy intake before the first BIZZY, audible, the kind you take when someone might be listening; a scuffed half-breath on the comma; no clean breath at the end — the phrase is interrupted by impact.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: The buzz-hum sits under the syllables continuously; a small grunt of effort compresses into the last BIZZY as the anthers dump their weight on him.
voicePerformances.physicalActionRelationship: Voice and body telling the same lie together: the syllables land on the up-beats of the porpoise so the song sounds like it is steering him, when the flight is steering the song. The final trailing syllable coincides with the flank meeting the leaf, so the tune gets bent by the bow rather than finished.

voicePerformances.breaths: One exhale carrying the crash out of his chest and converting it into the verdict; nothing after — he does not breathe again until the eye-flick.
voicePerformances.nonVerbalActions: Tiny catch of air on the 'd' of NAILED, the only sound the impact left in him.

voicePerformances.speaker: Fuzzby

showrunnerJudgement: PASSES. UNIVERSALS TEST run first: endingBehaviour is not templated — the leaf-ricochet cover, pollen reveal, Zenny’s long dead stop, the denied short reaction, the weather warning hold and the final flower clamp all end differently. cutPace is also not templated — 1.B1 preserves the chained physical cause, 1.B2 buys the long Zenny wall, 1.B3 withholds the expected hold, and 1.B4 lengthens under thunder. There is a shared card structure, but not a shared cinematic value asserting itself. I tried to reject this for repeated reaction grammar and safe coverage; it survives because the repetitions are the scene’s engine and each repeat changes power, duration or meaning. Fuzzby cannot be substituted out: the action is authored by his overcommitted body, his denial, and his need for Zenny’s witness. Zenny cannot be substituted out: the comedy depends on her almost-motionless withholding and the affection she refuses to confess. The scene has the Crystal Bears co-viewing shape: the child rides, crashes, laughs; the parent sees a whole performance flown for the one bee who will not budge, with the first weather ache arriving underneath the gag.
treatmentComparison: The storyboard holds the selected treatment’s central experience: bee-height travel with Fuzzby as the camera’s reckless partner, then hard grammatical collisions into Zenny’s unmoving frame. It preserves the key treatment promises: the opening already travels; the 1.B1 dip-drag-leaf FWIP remains one continuous cause; Zenny’s first verdict is a true door-shut rather than ordinary reaction coverage; 1.B3 escalates one object, the pollen, instead of adding random business; and 1.B4 brings the storm through the existing depth of the meadow rather than cutting to a safe re-establishing master. The visual grammar remains welded, not blended: Fuzzby’s shots chase, bank, arrive late or get thrown; Zenny’s shots flatten and refuse motion. The only near-risk is density: several shot cards are packed, but the packed material is still observable cause-and-effect rather than decorative micro-expression, so it does not yet tip into generic prompt stuffing.

producerFeasibility.judgement: Feasibility read only; no creative opinion offered on any shot. Both mechanical facts come back clean and I reason from them as given: every character named across the ten shots (Fuzzby, Zenny) has a locked anchor, so there is no missing-reference BLOCK anywhere in the scene, and all ten intended durations validate with a scene total of 71-97s. Cast scope is genuinely small — a two-character scene, never more than two named characters in one composition, and in every shot but one only one of them is actually performing, so each frame is a reference-anchored single-subject or clearly-staged two-subject composition well inside what this pipeline holds together. Fuzzby-anchor identity is carried through progressive face-covering (band in SH3, smear in SH5, cake in SH6, still caked in SH8/SH10), which is a real ask of the anchor rather than a scope problem, and the Production Detail already names the spectacles-must-read-through-the-gold requirement on each of those shots, so it is briefed rather than assumed. Two practical notes rather than blocks: SH1 asks for the largest single delivery in the scene — a 11-14s continuous corridor travel carrying a sung work-song, a chained multi-stage physical cause, and a deep-background second bee that must read at correct relative scale — and SH10 asks for a petal-fold-and-clamp practical effect that has no equivalent elsewhere in the scene to amortise against. Both are deliverable as written with the assets on disk; both are the shots where the scene's cost concentrates and are worth flagging to the schedule. Nothing here needs to stop; Gate 6b passes.

issues.issue: Longest shot in the scene (11-14s) and the heaviest single delivery: one unbroken travelling corridor flight carrying a sung work-song track, a multi-stage chained physical cause ending on the leaf FWIP, plus a deep-background second bee (Zenny) that must hold correct relative scale against Fuzzby at distance. Duration validates, and reference coverage is complete (Fuzzby anchor, Zenny anchor, size chart, Buzzing Nook/wildflower scene anchor), but this shot alone concentrates the scene's animation and take-count cost — the deep-background Zenny at small scale is the element most likely to need additional takes to hold identity and the size gap. Flagged for schedule, not for change.

Requires a petal fold-and-clamp practical — petals closing across the lens's view of Fuzzby and staying shut with only his rear half and two wings outside — with no comparable effect elsewhere in the scene to share setup cost with. Deliverable with the existing scene anchor and Scene Look, but it is a one-off effects cost sitting on the scene's second-longest duration (9-12s).

The frame must carry three independent physical elements the shot itself specifies as evidence — a branch still swinging in the mid-ground, kicking legs above a blossom rim with the body buried, and gold raining down a light shaft between camera and subject — before the haul-out and stance accent. Each is simulated/animated separately and all three must read cleanly in one composition at bee scale within 7-10s. No missing assets and the duration validates; noted only as the scene's third concentration of per-shot effects work.
